topic: Compile-Time Polymorphism via Template Metaprogramming and its Implementation
explanation: Template metaprogramming allows computations to be performed at compile time, leveraging the compiler's ability to generate specialized code for different template arguments. This contrasts with runtime polymorphism achieved through virtual functions.  The compiler's implementation involves recursive template instantiation, potentially leading to significant compile-time overhead for complex metaprograms.  Memory layout is directly influenced by the types deduced at compile time; there's no runtime overhead associated with virtual function calls or virtual function tables (vtables).  Assembly-level behavior reveals highly optimized code tailored to the specific types used, avoiding runtime branching and polymorphism mechanisms.  The trade-off is compile time versus runtime performance.
keywords: Static Polymorphism, Template Metaprogramming, Compile-Time Polymorphism
